title: Mineral Rights — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Ownership, Leasing and Division Order Worksheets: Mapping Mineral and Royalty Interests, Rebuilding Every Decimal, and Clearing Title Before Signing

worksheets.title: Ownership Map and Tract Inventory
worksheets.purpose: Build a verified, tract-by-tract record of what you actually own, separating mineral, royalty, NPRI, and override interests, converting every acre figure to net royalty acres, and tying each entry to a source deed and state well record.
instructions: Gather every deed, lease, division order, and royalty statement related to the minerals before filling any field, and keep everything that might be related.
Work one tract at a time, copying legal descriptions from the source deed rather than from a check stub or tax notice.
Express every interest three ways: net mineral acres, royalty decimal, and net royalty acres normalized to one-eighth.
Run the sum check on every tract and pull the deeds whenever owner decimals fail to add up to the lease royalty.
Redact Social Security numbers before any document touches an AI tool, and spot-check every AI-generated figure by hand.

fields.name: interest_type_classification
fields.prompt: List every interest you hold in each tract and label it as a mineral interest, royalty interest, non-participating royalty interest, or overriding royalty interest. Note which document created it, whether it carries the executive right, and whether it can collect bonus or rentals.
fields.example: Tract A, 40 gross acres in Reeves County: full mineral interest by 1952 deed, executive right included, so I lease and collect bonus. Tract B: a 1/16 NPRI, production only, no lease, bonus, or rentals. An NPRI can be sold for a lump sum while the mineral owner keeps control [Matt Sands — 3AnqzZSRGtg @ 00:11:29].

fields.name: nma_to_nra_conversion
fields.prompt: Convert your net mineral acres into net royalty acres using your actual lease royalty rate, then restate every per-acre offer you have received in dollars per net royalty acre so competing bids can be compared on the same one-eighth basis.
fields.example: 16 NMA under a 25% royalty equals 32 NRA because net royalty acres are normalized to one-eighth. A buyer offering $6,000 per NMA, or $96,000 total, is really paying only $3,000 per NRA. I logged both figures side by side before replying to the buyer's letter [Matt Sands — iVFjOPF8JW0 @ 00:09:06].

fields.name: lease_royalty_rate
fields.prompt: Record the royalty rate on each existing lease and, for unleased tracts, the rate a buyer or lessee assumes in its offer. Note the going rate in your area and whether a gap leaves room to negotiate before you respond.
fields.example: Tract C is unleased. The buyer's offer assumed a 12.5% royalty, but nearby leases are running 15-20%, so I asked which rate they used and countered [Matt Sands — iVFjOPF8JW0 @ 00:14:51]. Lease royalties typically run 12.5% to 25% of gross well revenue, paid monthly while the well produces [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — WZxmCcTgeWk @ 00:00:49].

fields.name: npri_fixed_or_floating
fields.prompt: Quote the exact NPRI wording from each reservation deed and decide whether it reads as a fixed fraction of production or a floating fraction of whatever royalty the lease sets. Calculate the NPRI decimal under both readings at your current lease royalty.
fields.example: The 1961 deed reserves 'one-half of the one-eighth royalty.' Read as fixed, it stays at one-sixteenth whether the lease royalty is one-eighth or 25%. Read as floating, it would be one-half of the royalty, or 12.5% on my 25% lease. In Van Dyke that difference was worth about $44 million [Oliva Gibbs — QPk4GTvt5YU @ 00:12:22].

fields.name: tract_sum_check
fields.prompt: Build a sum check for every tract: list each owner's royalty or NPRI decimal, add them together, and compare the total to the lease royalty. Record any shortfall or overage and which deeds you pulled to explain it.
fields.example: Tract B lease royalty is 25%. Ann holds 12.5% as mineral owner, Bob holds a 6.25% NPRI, and Carl was shown at 3.125%, totaling 21.875%. Ann plus Bob plus Carl has to equal the lease royalty, so I went back to the deeds to find the missing 3.125% [LMJ Land Services — IBxLIQjDNto @ 00:02:02].

fields.name: orri_status_and_valuation
fields.prompt: For any overriding royalty you hold or are considering, record the underlying lease, whether it is still alive, the producing wells holding it, protective language against washout, and the production basis you used to value it today.
fields.example: Offered a 1% ORRI on an old single-well lease. The override is carved from the working interest and dies if the lease is released, so I confirmed the well is economic and valued only existing production. I also requested anti-washout language in the assignment before agreeing to any price [Matt Sands — pjmqehPUgL8 @ 00:07:10].

fields.name: legal_description_and_gis_plot
fields.prompt: Copy the legal description for each tract directly from the source deed, plot it on the free state GIS map, and record the API numbers of every well and permit that falls inside or touches the tract boundary.
fields.example: Tract A legal description pulled from the 1952 deed and plotted on the Texas RRC viewer using 8-digit API entry. Two permitted laterals cross the section, and I confirmed the first take point and lateral footage fall inside my tract on the permit and plat before trusting the nearby pad [Matt Sands — gFgW6n9nb-c @ 00:13:20].

fields.name: state_data_sources
fields.prompt: Name the state data sites you use for each tract, the subscription or cost of each, and the production figures you pulled, noting whether volumes are reported by lease or by well and whether gas is wet or dry.
fields.example: North Dakota tract: skipped the $50-a-year DMR Basic subscription and used WellDatabase's free tier [Matt Sands — 1HDBzjGoDdc @ 00:16:47]. Texas tract: summed wells at the lease level and read the disposition column, since April 2012 showed 1,990 bbl produced but 1,905 sold. RRC gas is wet, so paid volume runs lower [Matt Sands — gFgW6n9nb-c @ 00:25:22].

fields.name: title_search_record
fields.prompt: Describe the title work completed on each tract, who performed it, what it cost, and how long it took. Note whether a dedicated mineral title search was run, since the mineral chain runs separately from the surface chain.
fields.example: Inherited Tract D: hired a landman at about $600 a day for a limited title search that cost roughly $3,000 and took about one week [Matt Sands — u4xA0UNrxQs @ 00:19:39]. The mineral chain was run on its own, separate from the surface, and it exposed a 1938 split-off [AFX Videos — JpHijIsWFL4 @ 00:01:50].

fields.name: master_inventory_and_ai_controls
fields.prompt: Describe the master spreadsheet that logs every tract with interest type, net acres, lease status, and provenance. Note any AI tools used to build run sheets, how you spot-checked their output, and what personal data you redacted first.
fields.example: One workbook, one row per tract: interest type, NMA, NRA, lease status, operator, and source deed. I fed division orders to a paid AI tier with training opt-out, after redacting my Social Security number, then spot-checked every decimal by hand. Every related paper stays in a labeled folder for my heirs [Matt Sands — NkT15qxxGYM @ 00:34:48].

worksheets.completion_gate: Every tract has a source deed, an interest type, net mineral acres, net royalty acres, a lease status, and a passing sum check; every offer on file has been converted to dollars per net royalty acre; and every NPRI and ORRI has a written fixed-or-floating or lease-alive determination.

worksheets.title: Lease Terms, Pooling Math and Net Revenue Interest
worksheets.purpose: Judge every lease and pooling decision on royalty economics rather than bonus headlines, and rebuild owner and operator net revenue interests from acres, royalty fractions, and burdens so no decimal is accepted on faith.
instructions: Negotiate before signing; once a lease is executed, its royalty, shut-in, and pooling terms may govern for 20, 30, or 50 years.
Read the full lease, including strike-outs and addenda, before entering any royalty rate.
Write every calculation as fractions first, then decimals, showing acres, unit size, and royalty rate as separate inputs.
Calendar every election deadline and shut-in payment date the day the notice or lease arrives.
Check each lease separately when a unit combines leases with different burdens, and sum back to the tract share.

fields.name: royalty_versus_bonus
fields.prompt: Compare each lease offer's bonus against its royalty rate and estimate the long-term value of every extra point of royalty. Record whether you would accept a lower or zero bonus in exchange for the highest available royalty, and why.
fields.example: Offer 1: $1,500 per acre bonus at 1/5. Offer 2: zero bonus at 25%. Sands says it is almost always better to take zero bonus and the highest royalty because the rate drives mineral value going forward [Matt Sands — qru8bh4mMms @ 00:09:06]. Still, a zero bonus can signal an operator not serious about drilling [Energy Law Professor — WBGDgooXnq8 @ 00:22:32].

fields.name: bonus_benchmark
fields.prompt: Estimate the current value per net mineral acre for each tract, divide it by two and by three to set a fair bonus range, and compare that range to the bonus actually offered in writing by each landman or operator.
fields.example: Nacogdoches County Haynesville tract, 14.3 NMA, offered $300 per NMA. Minerals valued near $3,000 per NMA support about a $1,000 per acre bonus using the divide-by-two-or-three rule [Matt Sands — xiP5PiaaYKE @ 00:06:17]. I pulled competing terms from the Lease Price Report and Mineral Rights Forum before countering [Matt Sands — xiP5PiaaYKE @ 00:09:06].

fields.name: lease_face_and_addenda_check
fields.prompt: Read every page of each existing lease, including strike-outs, interlineations, and addenda, and record the royalty rate that actually controls. If only a memorandum of lease is recorded, note how you obtained or back-calculated the real terms.
fields.example: The printed form says 1/8, but like the 1998 Jim Wells County lease where 1/8 was struck and replaced with 1/5, my addendum sets 19% and overrides the printed 12.5% [Tracy Lenz — HGUBxgz_6Ak @ 00:22:21]. A second tract shows only a memorandum, so I back-calculated royalty from three of the four variables on the check [Tracy Lenz — HGUBxgz_6Ak @ 00:13:01].

fields.name: shut_in_clause_log
fields.prompt: Quote the shut-in royalty clause from each lease, note whether it covers gas wells only or all wells, list the payment due dates, and record whether every shut-in payment arrived on time, since a late payment can end the lease.
fields.example: Lease 2 has a 'gas well' shut-in clause, so it cannot hold an oil well shut in for low prices [Energy Law Professor — 7sPTlHr4F7A @ 00:12:56]. Its language keeps the lease 'while royalty is so paid,' and in Freeman v. Magnolia a late payment terminated the lease. I log every payment date [Energy Law Professor — 7sPTlHr4F7A @ 00:07:22].

fields.name: pooled_tract_dilution
fields.prompt: For each pooled unit, multiply your lease royalty by your tract acres over total unit acres and write down the resulting decimal. Compare it with the headline royalty rate so you value the interest on what it actually pays.
fields.example: My 5-acre tract sits in a 40-acre pooled unit under a 3/16 lease. The math is 3/16 x 5/40 = .0234375, really about 2% rather than the 18% the lease face suggests. I now value this tract on the .0234375 decimal, not the headline royalty rate [behoge13 — le24nqd0H0M @ 00:13:55].

fields.name: force_pooling_election
fields.prompt: If you received a force-pooling order or notice, record the election options offered, the written election deadline, the risk penalty attached to each option, and the default deemed-lease terms that apply if no election is made.
fields.example: Notice received for a $6M well. Option two carries a 300% risk penalty, meaning $18M of production is recovered before payout, and reworks reset it. Default with no election is a deemed lease at $300 per acre and 1/8. I mailed my election in writing ten days early [behoge13 — le24nqd0H0M @ 00:37:31].

fields.name: leverage_and_holdout_risk
fields.prompt: Describe your leverage on each tract, including your net acreage relative to the unit size, nearby delineation results, and any offers you have declined. Record what you would lose if drilling moved elsewhere while you held out for better terms.
fields.example: I own 5 net acres inside a 1,280-acre unit, so I am more likely to be pooled than to dictate terms; 5,000-acre owners command 1/4 cost-free royalties. During the Haynesville rush bonuses hit $20,000 per acre, yet holdouts lost multi-million-dollar offers once delineation drilling proved their acreage worthless [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — hZZNvuvGfkc @ 00:02:04].

fields.name: owner_nri_decimal
fields.prompt: Calculate your owner net revenue interest for each well by dividing net mineral acres by drilling spacing unit acres and multiplying by the lease royalty. Then estimate an early royalty check using expected volumes and a realistic realized price.
fields.example: Bakken tract: 16 NMA divided by a 1,280-acre DSU times a 15% royalty gives .001875 [Matt Sands — Yy7az5T7_vs @ 00:12:22]. Nearby wells averaged 10,000 barrels in three months; at $50 per barrel, not the $60 WTI print, that is about $937. State data can lag a couple of months [Matt Sands — Yy7az5T7_vs @ 00:16:47].

fields.name: operator_nri_and_overrides
fields.prompt: Work out the operator's net revenue interest on each lease by subtracting the royalty and every override from its working interest, then carry that lease-level figure into the unit by tract share. Run the check lease by lease.
fields.example: A 1/8 lease leaves the operator 0.875 and a 3/16 lease leaves 0.8125. On the Sunrise lease, 100% WI minus a 12.5% royalty and 5% geologist override leaves 82.5 cents per dollar; pooled as 80 acres into 320, that is a 0.20625 unit NRI. I checked each lease separately, never commingled [UHD Continuing and Professional Education — oHKF06pFkh0 @ 00:10:21].

fields.name: npri_and_unleased_trap
fields.prompt: Identify any conveyance using 'produced and saved' or similar royalty language, record the NPRI it created, and note whether a lease exists yet. Keep mineral interest in its own spreadsheet column rather than folding it into acres.
fields.example: The 1974 deed to Charlie reads 'produced and saved,' so Charlie holds a 3% NPRI, not minerals. With no lease yet, David owns 100% of the minerals subject to that NPRI, and the answer is not 9.5% [Land Training www.landtraining.net — HkEK5QVZAJ0 @ 00:04:30]. Mineral interest sits in its own column so a bad input stays visible.

worksheets.completion_gate: Every lease offer has a bonus benchmark and a royalty comparison, every pooled tract has a royalty-times-tract-share decimal, every force-pooling notice has a written election or a recorded decision to default, and every owner and operator NRI reconciles lease by lease.

worksheets.title: Division Order Audit and Title Curative Log
worksheets.purpose: Verify the decimal on every division order and check stub before signing, control the paper you return to each operator, and document the title chain and curative steps needed to release suspended royalties.
instructions: Do not sign any division order until your rebuilt decimal matches the operator's figure or the operator has shown its calculation in writing.
Treat a division order as a statement of your decimal, not a lease amendment, and strike language that changes lease terms.
Return the W-9 to every payer whether or not you sign the order.
Run title in fractions from the earliest conveyance forward, flagging 'of my interest' wording and never guessing.
Price every curative step against the value of the interest and ask the operator what it will accept before drafting.

fields.name: rebuilt_decimal
fields.prompt: Rebuild the decimal for each well on the division order from your own records: net mineral acres divided by unit acres, multiplied by the lease royalty rate. Record the operator's decimal beside yours and the difference between them.
fields.example: Two-section horizontal unit under a 3/16 lease: 160 NMA divided by 1,280 acres times 18.75% equals 0.0234375, and that exact number should appear for every well in the unit [Matt Sands — tJr4jiz31fw @ 00:15:50]. The operator showed 0.0234375 on wells one and two, so both matched before I signed anything.

fields.name: discrepancy_cost
fields.prompt: When your rebuilt decimal and the operator's decimal differ, calculate the monthly, yearly, and long-term dollar gap using the well's current gross revenue, and note whether the gap is a real error or only rounding at the eighth decimal place.
fields.example: Correct decimal 0.015625, order shows 0.0078125. On a well generating $100,000 a month, that gap costs $781.25 monthly, $9,375 yearly, and $187,500 over a simplified 20 years [Mineral View — KYu7M4t5LAk @ 00:02:08]. By contrast, a miss at the eighth decimal place is one penny per million dollars of revenue [Matt Sands — tJr4jiz31fw @ 00:29:18].

fields.name: stub_versus_lease_fraction
fields.prompt: Hold the decimal printed on each royalty check stub against the lease royalty fraction and your rebuilt decimal. Note whether the stub reflects an outdated one-eighth figure, a pooled tract share, or another basis you cannot yet explain.
fields.example: My lease is 1/4, but the stub decimal matches the old 1/8 calculation, which pays exactly half of a 1/4 royalty, so I am being paid half [Royalty Clerk — blbomhUd0sA @ 00:01:11]. Running the math backward, the stub credits me with 20 acres instead of 40, so I called the land department before signing [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — Z_HlEDh8-rw @ 00:08:30].

fields.name: struck_clauses_and_delivery
fields.prompt: List every clause on the division order that goes beyond the statutory contents for your state, mark which ones you struck and initialed, and record how and when you returned the order with proof of delivery.
fields.example: Texas order included an indemnity clause and post-production cost language. I struck both, initialed each strike with a line saying I do not agree, and returned it by a method giving proof of delivery [Royalty Clerk — DN-VIoSmyF0 @ 00:03:58]. If the payer balks, it may not withhold payment solely because I refused provisions beyond the list [Royalty Clerk — DN-VIoSmyF0 @ 00:01:56].

fields.name: form_choice_by_operator
fields.prompt: Decide for each operator whether you will sign its form, substitute the NADOA model division order, or decline to sign at all. Record the objectionable language, the operator's response, and any state late-payment remedies that apply.
fields.example: Texas operator's form carried cost-deduction terms against my cost-free lease, so I sent the NADOA model form; Blue Mesa had problems with maybe 2 of about 130 operators [Blue Mesa Minerals — SfX6ycoYg24 @ 00:06:26]. On the Oklahoma well I signed nothing, citing Hull v. Sun Refining and 12% interest compounded annually on late pay [Richard Winblad — iD4uCjptCXM @ 00:09:58].

fields.name: w9_and_withholding_status
fields.prompt: Confirm a signed W-9 and tax ID are on file with every payer, including operators whose division orders you refuse to sign. Record the date each was sent and whether any backup withholding has appeared on your statements.
fields.example: W-9 mailed to all three operators on the same day, including the Oklahoma operator whose division order I declined, so no company withholds the maximum the tax code requires [Richard Winblad — iD4uCjptCXM @ 00:09:16]. Without it, backup withholding runs roughly 28%. I logged the send dates and confirmed no withholding appeared on the first statements.

fields.name: operator_change_red_flag
fields.prompt: When a well changes operators or a new division order arrives, compare its decimal with the prior order. If the number moved, record your written request for the operator's calculation and any redacted title opinion pages covering your interest.
fields.example: New operator's order dropped my decimal, which is a red flag, so I asked in writing how it came up with the number [Matt Sands — tJr4jiz31fw @ 00:35:55]. I also requested the one or two redacted title opinion pages mentioning my interest, which show exactly how the decimal was built [Matt Sands — tJr4jiz31fw @ 00:24:58].

fields.name: courthouse_search_log
fields.prompt: Log each courthouse or online records search you ran, including the platform, search terms, number of results, cost, and turnaround. Note any zero-result searches and how you ruled out an input error before concluding nothing was recorded.
fields.example: Reeves County legal-description search on Courthouse Direct returned 439 results for $63.90, a $20 base plus $0.10 per record [CourthouseAcademy — 822U1_i8V5Q @ 00:21:12]. A first attempt returned zero because data went into the wrong box, so I re-entered it [CourthouseAcademy — 822U1_i8V5Q @ 00:20:42]. A complex chain may take 3-5 weeks [Matt Sands — zoP-dgL5D7M @ 00:11:42].

fields.name: fraction_chain_verification
fields.prompt: Work every conveyance in the chain as a fraction, flag any deed containing the words 'of my interest,' and show how each grantor's share passed forward. Record who verified each fraction so no interest leaves the desk as a guess.
fields.example: Grandfather owned 1/2 and deeded 'one-half of my interest' to Aunt Ruth, so she received 1/4, not 1/2, because a grantor can only deed out what they have [Sebastian Cosme — -fWjBQtg9r4 @ 00:01:35]. A second reviewer verified every fraction, since guessed title calls have produced $400,000 to $500,000 mistakes [Landman Class — ibeQr-rDmZ4 @ 00:35:50].

fields.name: curative_plan_and_cost
fields.prompt: For each title defect, describe the curative instrument you plan to use, what the operator or division order analyst said it will accept, the estimated cost, and how that cost compares with the value of the interest.
fields.example: Uncle's 0.1 net-acre interest is in suspense. A simple probate would run $3,000-4,000 and could exceed its value, so I asked the division order analyst first and they will accept an affidavit of heirship [Matt Sands — sB8BNPnN_Os @ 00:16:13]. One signed lease lacked trustee capacity, so I re-obtained the signature rather than editing it [Susan Jessup — sldaaowniGM @ 00:32:23].

worksheets.completion_gate: Every well has a rebuilt decimal matching the operator's or a written dispute on file, every returned order has documented strikes and proof of delivery, every payer has a W-9, and every title defect has a costed curative plan the operator has agreed to accept.

worksheets.title: Wells, Decline Curves and What Your Producing Minerals Are Worth
worksheets.purpose: Build a working record of how the wells under your tract were drilled, how fast they are declining, and what that decline means for value. Turn rig schedules, lateral footage, decline settings, and economic limits into a defensible valuation before you answer any offer.
instructions: Pull the drilling permit, plat, and completion records for every well touching your tract before filling in any field, and keep copies in the same folder as your deeds.
Separate producing wells from permitted or proposed wells, and complete the decline and economic limit fields only for wells with real production history.
Exclude early flowback from any decline fit and wait for 18 to 24 months of unrestricted production before trusting a single well's own curve.
Divide any bundled first check by the number of production months it covers before using it to budget or to value the interest.
Treat every valuation figure as a range, and record the multiple, discount, price, and decline assumptions next to the number so another reader can reproduce it.

fields.name: well_type_and_pad_layout
fields.prompt: Describe the well type drilling your tract, whether vertical, deviated, directional, or horizontal, and record how many wells share the pad. Note the spacing unit acreage and whether one multi-well pad replaced multiple vertical locations across the section you hold.
fields.example: Our 1,280-acre section is developed from one horizontal pad. Chesapeake's field comparison shows up to 32 vertical wells on separate pads replaced by a single multi-well horizontal pad with 90% less surface disturbance [Oil & Gas Industry VDA — 7tXxUXv528A @ 00:05:10]. We logged four horizontal wells on the pad, all producing from the same unit, and mapped the pad.

fields.name: rig_timeline
fields.prompt: Record the rig schedule for the wells on or near your tract, including spud date, total depth date, and expected rig days. Compare the operator's actual pace against the typical continuous drilling window so you can anticipate when completion and first production may follow.
fields.example: Expand Energy drills a typical horizontal natural gas well 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for approximately 21 to 28 days [Expand Energy — zhTs0NrEVgE @ 00:00:16]. Our permit showed a spud in early March, so we penciled total depth for late March and set a reminder to check for completion activity and the first royalty statement afterward.

fields.name: lateral_length_and_trajectory
fields.prompt: Enter the permitted lateral length and describe how the wellbore turns from vertical to horizontal, including whether a rotary steerable system or bent motor is named. Note how much of the lateral footage actually crosses your tract according to the plat.
fields.example: The build curve can be steered using either a rotary steerable system or a downhole motor assembly with an adjustable bend [Expand Energy — zhTs0NrEVgE @ 00:03:57]. Our Utica permit lists a lateral longer than 12,500 ft, matching nearly nine out of 10 wells drilled in 2025 [FutureWise Energy — nbj7-lPJ59w @ 00:11:46]. Roughly a third crosses our tract.

fields.name: pad_capital_and_operator_commitment
fields.prompt: Estimate the upfront capital the operator has committed to the pad or wells affecting your minerals. Record the source of the figure and explain what that spending suggests about how seriously the operator intends to develop the remaining locations in your unit.
fields.example: Range Resources puts upfront investment for a single Marcellus drilling pad upwards of $60 million, maybe even $70 million, before a blade of grass is moved [Range Resources Corporation — 8M30VzyjEpk @ 00:01:53]. We treated that scale of commitment as evidence the operator plans to keep drilling the pad, and we tracked whether new permits followed.

fields.name: bench_and_zone_screening
fields.prompt: List every target zone or bench beneath your tract and describe what evidence supports each one. Record whether physical cuttings, open-hole logs, or offset results were reviewed, and flag any zone where the evidence is thin or the logs alone carry the case.
fields.example: Premier analyzed four Wolfcamp wells in Eddy and Lee County and found two great, one marginal and one poor, even though the open hole logs looked fairly similar [Hart Energy — KynEhshipEg @ 00:07:18]. Our tract has two candidate benches supported only by logs, so we marked both as unproven until cuttings or offset production confirm them.

fields.name: first_check_reality
fields.prompt: Record the production months covered by your first royalty check and calculate what a single month actually paid. Write down how you will budget household spending until several single-month checks show the real run rate rather than the bundled opening payment.
fields.example: Troy Eckard warns that the first check covers one to five months of production, and the next single-month check can run a third or a sixth of it [Eckard Enterprises | Oil & Gas Investing — nn1juJ3_-WA @ 00:08:21]. Our first check covered four months, so we divided it by four and budgeted household spending only from that smaller monthly figure.

fields.name: decline_profile
fields.prompt: Describe the decline profile of the producing wells on your tract, including the share of volume expected in the first two years. Record whether the data comes from your own statements, state production reports, or a type curve built from offset wells.
fields.example: A shale well will recover 70 to 80 percent of its total volume within the first two years of production [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — CiR-w5lHfvI @ 00:11:46]. Our two wells came online eighteen months ago, so we assumed most of their volume has already been produced and reduced our expectations for future checks accordingly, pending new drilling.

fields.name: decline_fit_settings
fields.prompt: Document the settings you used to fit a decline curve, including the b-factor cap, terminal decline rate, start point, and months of data. Explain how you excluded flowback and why the well has enough unrestricted history to support a forecast.
fields.example: We kept the b-factor below 1.3 with an 8% terminal decline, which Matt Sands calls a good conservative number for most wells [Matt Sands — VYytHJ0lMVw @ 00:38:39]. We moved the start marker past early flowback before running the hyperbolic regression [KAPPA Engineering — tPB4O0ryZww @ 00:01:54], and used 22 months of unrestricted production, satisfying the 18-24 month minimum before trusting the fitted curve.

fields.name: economic_limit
fields.prompt: Calculate the economic limit rate where revenue from oil and gas equals operating cost for the producing well. Record the oil price, net gas price, gas-oil ratio, and operating expense you used, and note how close current production sits to that breakeven.
fields.example: TopDogEngineer solved q times oil price plus q times GOR times gas price minus OpEx equals zero, using a net gas price of about $2.067/Mcf, and reached 140.3 bbl/month [TopDogEngineer — 4mzbNb16NQc @ 00:08:25]. Below that rate the well loses money, so we flagged our older well producing roughly 200 bbl/month for close monthly watching.

fields.name: valuation_snapshot
fields.prompt: Produce a quick valuation of your producing royalty using a multiple of recent monthly income, then explain how development timing, price assumptions, and decline would change that number. Note whether a full engineering valuation should follow before any offer is considered.
fields.example: Matt Sands values mature producing minerals at 50 to 70 times the average of the last 3 months of royalty, up to 100 times in hot areas [Matt Sands — 86mQK92f7Bg @ 00:29:36]. Our three-month average was $1,200, giving a quick range of $60,000 to $84,000 before a full engineering valuation tests decline and development timing.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not move to Worksheet 5 until every producing well has a documented decline fit built on 18 to 24 months of unrestricted data with flowback excluded, the first check has been divided into single production months, an economic limit rate is recorded, and the quick valuation lists its multiple and assumptions.

worksheets.title: Selling, Taxes and Passing Minerals to Heirs
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether to hold or sell with a clear view of development stage, lease royalty rate, buyer quality, and deal paperwork, then lock in the tax and inheritance steps that keep royalties flowing. Use it to protect value at sale, at filing time, and at death.
instructions: Write down your reason for selling before you contact any buyer, and list the tracts you would keep for future development upside.
Research every buyer through recently recorded mineral deeds and online presence, and discard unsolicited mail that resembles a check, legal agreement, or deed.
Have the purchase and sale agreement and the deed reviewed at your own expense for any language reaching royalties in suspense or escheated funds.
Confirm a W-9 and tax ID are on file with every operator, choose a depletion method property by property, and keep every receipt for deductible mineral expenses.
Record every county and state where minerals sit so heirs know exactly where to file affidavits of heirship and which operators to contact.

fields.name: reason_to_sell_or_hold
fields.prompt: State plainly why you are considering a sale, whether for liquidity, estate simplicity, or risk transfer. Describe what price and volume risk you would hand to a buyer, and what future development upside you would give up by accepting a lump sum.
fields.example: Steven Hatcher says selling shifts the price risk and the volume risk over to the buyer [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — Sz-1-E8zTqU @ 00:05:01], and that selling is choosing the lower lump sum. We want liquidity for a family expense, so we wrote down which tracts we would sell and which tracts with upside we would keep.

fields.name: development_stage_discount
fields.prompt: Classify each tract by development stage, from producing wells to rig on site to acreage inside an operator's five-year plan. Assign the discount rate a buyer is likely to apply at each stage and explain how that changes the offer you should expect.
fields.example: Matt Sands discounts producing minerals at about 10%, rig-on-site acreage at 15-20%, and acreage inside an SEC five-year plan at 20-30% [Modern Land Investor — 1c2UBDuXhrk @ 00:33:41]. Our north tract produces, so we expect the tightest discount there, while the south tract sits in a five-year plan and will draw a much steeper one.

fields.name: lease_rate_before_sale
fields.prompt: Record the royalty rate on any existing lease, or the rate you could negotiate before selling unleased acreage. Explain how the rate changes what a buyer will pay, and decide whether leasing first at a stronger royalty would raise the eventual sale price.
fields.example: A 25% royalty yields twice the sale value of a 12.5% royalty [Matt Sands — RR2BlQf14H8 @ 00:05:59]. In Reeves, Lea and Eddy counties, Sands advises leasing before selling, because taking a 12% royalty instead of 25% halves the property's value. Our Reeves County acreage is unleased, so we will lease first and price the sale afterward.

fields.name: buyer_screening
fields.prompt: List every buyer who has contacted you and how each one reached you. For each, record whether they are visible online, whether they pressured you, whether their mail looked like a check or deed, and whether recent recorded deeds show them actively buying.
fields.example: Hatcher says to trash unsolicited mail that looks like a check, legal agreement or deed, and walk from any buyer who is evasive, invisible online or using high-pressure tactics [Steven Hatcher | Minerals Guy — WIqkczvqoz0 @ 00:05:35]. We pulled deeds recorded in the past 6-12 months to find active end buyers and dropped two evasive mail-only buyers [Matt Sands — y5etlsUEcO0 @ 00:32:43].

fields.name: psa_and_deed_review
fields.prompt: Review the purchase and sale agreement and draft deed line by line. Record any language that sweeps in royalties held in suspense or escheated funds, note who drafted the deed, and confirm whether you paid for your own independent review before signing.
fields.example: Sands warns that buyer-drafted deeds can sweep in suspense or escheated funds [Matt Sands — 86mQK92f7Bg @ 00:27:15]. Our draft PSA contained a sentence assigning all royalties in suspense to the buyer, so we paid for our own review, had that sentence struck, and confirmed the deed covered only the intended tracts before signing [Matt Sands — y5etlsUEcO0 @ 00:21:34].

fields.name: closing_mechanics_and_title
fields.prompt: Describe how the sale will close, including when a landman is hired, how title will be chained, and how payment will arrive. Note any adjustment to price if the landman finds fewer net acres than the purchase agreement assumed at signing.
fields.example: The buyer hires the landman only after a signed purchase and sale agreement, then adjusts the price to the net acres actually found [Cashflow Ninja — uhffuS4DlLQ @ 00:34:38]. No escrow companies will go near mineral rights, so our sale ends with a signed deed and a wire, and Blue Mesa usually closes inside a week.

fields.name: depletion_method
fields.prompt: For each property, choose percentage or cost depletion and record why. Note your basis, whether an appraisal is needed for an inherited asset, and how the chosen method will continue or stop once basis reaches zero in later tax years.
fields.example: Tracy Lenz says you don't have to use the same method for each property [Tracy Lenz — NYvxAlVlAmQ @ 00:22:40]. We used cost depletion on the freshly inherited tract with newly drilled wells, supported by an appraisal costing a couple thousand dollars, and 15% percentage depletion of gross on older royalties, which keeps running after basis hits zero [Tracy Lenz — NYvxAlVlAmQ @ 00:46:35].

fields.name: tax_id_and_deductions
fields.prompt: Confirm that a W-9 and tax ID are on file with every operator paying you. List deductible expenses tied to your minerals, such as attorney deed filings, landman research, and consulting fees, and record where the receipts are stored for filing.
fields.example: Operators are required to withhold about 30% when no W-9 or tax ID is on file [Matt Sands — _MHogbd2xzU @ 00:16:53]. We sent W-9s to all three operators before first production, confirmed receipt with each payer, and keep a labeled folder of attorney deed filing, landman research and consulting receipts for our preparer, all deductible [Matt Sands — z9gHz7FYvRk @ 00:09:45].

fields.name: working_interest_risk
fields.prompt: If a working interest is offered, compare its costs and tax treatment against your royalty position. Record plugging liability, non-consent penalties, the sponsor's track record and own money in the deal, and when K-1s are expected so filing can be planned.
fields.example: Lenz prices plugging and abandonment at $30,000 to $40,000 per well and flags the roughly 300% non-consent penalty [Tracy Lenz — mHolW0RfGQ0 @ 00:09:41]. The sponsor offering us a non-op interest had no 5 to 10 year track record, matching the warning about 4x to 5x markups that shrink $100,000 to $20,000 of real interest [Passive Income MD — 41VgsNOdrto @ 00:17:03], so we declined.

fields.name: heirship_and_transfer_plan
fields.prompt: Map how the minerals pass to heirs, listing every county and state where interests sit. Record whether an affidavit of heirship has been recorded in each county, which operators hold royalties in suspense, and what written instructions your heirs will receive.
fields.example: After a death, record the affidavit of heirship in every county where minerals sit, send each operator the packet with death certificate and W-9s, and ask in writing how much has been held [Royalty Clerk — q5XqULtWaUQ @ 00:04:03]. Our minerals sit in two states, so we budgeted several thousand dollars per state to clear suspense.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not move to Worksheet 6 until every tract carries a development-stage discount, every buyer has been screened against recorded deeds, the PSA and deed have had your own review for suspense language, W-9s are confirmed with every operator, and an heirship map lists every county and state.

worksheets.title: Regulators, Hearings and the Mineral Market
worksheets.purpose: Track the permits, dockets, bonding rules, and market forces that decide when and how your minerals get paid. Connect regulator activity, gas quality, price lag, operator capital allocation, deductions, and emerging opportunities to concrete actions you take on your own acreage.
instructions: Search the state regulator portal and GIS viewer for every permit and docket item touching your unit, and save each permit, plat, and case record.
Calendar every hearing date and protest deadline as soon as you find it, because the docket clock controls the outcome.
Assess your operator's bonding exposure and inactive well count, and note any plugging cost figures raised in rulemaking or public comment.
Compare each royalty statement against the lease for deductions and against the price month it reflects, and never budget household spending on spot prices.
Screen every new lease, easement, or helium offer for counterparty track record, and bring a landman or attorney before accepting any final offer.

fields.name: permit_and_api_lookup
fields.prompt: Record every drilling permit affecting your tract, including the W-1 or state equivalent, the API number, permit date, and operator name. Note which regulator portal or GIS viewer you used and where the permit and plat copies are saved for later reference.
fields.example: We searched the RRC GIS viewer and RRC CASES portal for permits on our section and saved two W-1 permits with their plats. Before trusting a nearby pad, Sands says to pull the permit and plat and confirm the first take point and lateral footage fall inside your tract [Matt Sands — gFgW6n9nb-c @ 00:13:20].

fields.name: spacing_and_hearing_docket
fields.prompt: List any spacing, pooling, or permit hearings on the regulator's docket that touch your unit. Record the case number, hearing date, applicant, proposed well spacing, and the deadline for filing a protest or appearance so you do not miss the docket clock.
fields.example: At an OCD hearing, a witness said that if we were at much tighter spacings, we would be having a different conversation here, but that's not what we've proposed [OCD Pecos Hall — Gyi9ijeMNgA @ 00:48:28]. We logged the case, the hearing date and the proposed spacing for our unit, and set a calendar alert ahead of the protest deadline.

fields.name: child_well_and_parent_impact
fields.prompt: Identify any parent wells already producing near new child wells proposed for your unit. Describe how the operator's spacing and zone placement might affect performance, and record whether you plan to ask about parent wellbores within the same geologic zone.
fields.example: Enverus states plainly that child wells are significantly impacted [Enverus — 2rbY0Lt22CU @ 00:02:50], and its cylindrical search is a good proxy for considering parent wellbores within the same geologic zone [Enverus — hYa6oTD7seU @ 00:08:50]. Two older parent wells sit beside the proposed child wells in our unit, so we lowered our expected volumes for the new wells accordingly.

fields.name: operator_bonding_and_plugging_exposure
fields.prompt: Assess the operator's bonding and plugging exposure across its well count. Record how many of its wells are marginal or inactive, the bond tier that applies, and whether a stricter trigger could push the operator to abandon wells on or near your tract.
fields.example: McGowan's worked example shows a 100-well operator with 15 marginal or inactive wells facing a $15 million blanket bond overnight, with operators liable to hand you the keys and walk off [New Mexico Oil Conservation Commission — gfqoliQ78bk @ 00:54:15]. Our small operator runs about 60 wells, so we tallied its inactive count against that 15% trigger.

fields.name: plugging_cost_and_public_comment
fields.prompt: Record the plugging cost estimates raised in public comment or rulemaking for wells in your area. Note who presented each figure, whether it reflects an average or extreme case, and how orphaned wells could affect surface use or future development on your tract.
fields.example: Rossi of Moms Clean Air Force cited an average plugging cost of $163,000 per well, some over $700,000, with up to $1.6 billion unfunded [New Mexico Oil Conservation Commission — -7pNwWErBfk @ 00:01:06]. We recorded that figure as an advocate's average, separate from operator estimates, and noted two idle wells near our south boundary for follow-up with the regulator.

fields.name: gas_quality_and_takeaway
fields.prompt: Describe the gas composition and takeaway capacity for wells on your unit, including sour gas or impurity levels against pipeline limits. Record any allocation method the operator uses for impurities and whether midstream constraints could curtail production or delay royalty payments.
fields.example: Devon faced roughly 13,500 ppm sour gas against a 10,000 ppm takeaway allowance [OCD Pecos Hall — Gyi9ijeMNgA @ 00:34:55], and the workaround used gas samples for per-well impurity allocation and blended in leaner wells to dilute the stream. We asked our operator for the impurity reading on our wells and the allocation method it applies.

fields.name: price_lag_and_budget
fields.prompt: Track how commodity price moves reach your royalty statements. Record the months between a price spike and the check that reflects it, the weighted average price shown on the statement, and how you will avoid budgeting household spending on spot prints.
fields.example: Sands warns against budgeting household spending on spot spikes, because royalty statements reflect a monthly weighted average, not the instantaneous spot print [Matt Sands — M3eFdVkW_mY @ 00:03:56]. Price spikes reach checks about two months late, so after a spring rally we held spending flat until the statement showed the realized average for that production month.

fields.name: operator_capital_allocation
fields.prompt: Read your operator's latest investor presentation and record where windfall cash is going, whether to buybacks, dividends, acquisitions, or new drilling. Estimate how long before any rig response reaches your unit and note whether bolt-on deals suggest more activity nearby.
fields.example: Sands advises reading your operator's investor presentation instead of headlines [Matt Sands — n2MrqKJ_h80 @ 00:18:14] and expects at least a one to two quarter lag before rigs respond. Permian Resources ran about $1.05B across about 190 bolt-on deals year-to-date, the largest a $520M Ward County deal [The Byte-Size Brief — fqGTqf-VpBc @ 00:06:14], so we watched for new permits near our Ward County tract.

fields.name: deduction_and_easement_check
fields.prompt: Compare the post-production deductions on your statements against what your lease authorizes, and record any pipeline easement offers received. For each, note the amount, the offering company, the deduction or easement language, and whether a landman or attorney has reviewed it.
fields.example: Flywheel deducted post-production costs since 2019 under the net-proceeds statute despite gross proceeds leases, and only a court ruling stopped it [Matt Sands — n2MrqKJ_h80 @ 00:07:01]. Matterhorn's $21,000 final offer became a $7M jury award, though typical protesters win only 10% to 20% above the final offer [Matt Sands — FDXztudBSFk @ 00:10:24]. We brought an attorney to our easement offer.

fields.name: emerging_opportunity_screen
fields.prompt: Screen your acreage for emerging opportunities such as helium, carbon dioxide, or enhanced recovery. Record any scout card entries, prospect metrics, and the promoter's identity, and confirm whether the counterparty actually drills wells or simply re-promotes leases to others.
fields.example: Sands suggests scanning scout cards for non-flammable gas entries to find overlooked helium and CO2 potential [Matt Sands — ptrz57qzl54 @ 00:35:35]. Tim Rynott screens for 0.5% to 1.5% helium, 3 to 6 MMcf/d and 10 to 20 locations. A helium lease offer arrived from a company with no drilling history, so we declined it as a re-promoter.

worksheets.completion_gate: Treat this worksheet as complete only when every permit and plat is saved with its API number, every docket deadline is calendared, operator bonding exposure is tallied, statement deductions are checked against the lease, and every easement or helium offer has a named reviewer and a documented counterparty track record.
